text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, even for someone who did not write it. One key habit is following naming conventions. This means choosing clear, meaningful names for variables and functions, so readers quickly know what they do. Another good practice is keeping functions small and focused on a single task. When a function does too many things, it becomes hard to follow. Clean code is also easier to maintain. Fixing bugs or adding new features takes less time when the code is well organised. In short, writing clean code saves effort for everyone in the long run.
